svg.text: Not an app for reading disaster data. A community
service where villagers report changes in nature by
voice, read their village on a map, and know when to
prepare, when to leave, and where to go. The home page
answers “what is happening now”; a bubble answers “what
it means for me”; the next page answers “what do I do”.

text.font-family: EB Garamond, Cormorant Garamond, Times New Roman, serif

g.text: Only what you said is recorded. The app sorts it; it
never adds what you did not report.

svg.text: Hold, speak, release. The app drafts a structured
observation, but the villager confirms it. It records
only what was said: “muddier” never becomes “rising
fast”.

Why — a duller roar and yellow water usually mean
more water and silt coming from upstream.

svg.text: Tap any circle on the map. Solid glow = verified,
colour = level; dashed ring = unverified. The old
saying, and why it works, lives here, not on the home
page.

official warnings are labelled apart, with issuer and
time. Then: why, where, what to do, who needs help,
where to go.

to enter, where the water, toilets, beds and first aid
are, and which parts suit people who move slowly.

svg.text: Landmarks instead of compass directions: “turn left at
the Village Committee” is easier than “go 200 m north”.
Closed roads, a backup route, time at your own pace.
